findings.title: State-changing unsubscribe exposed over GET (CSRF / embedded-image muting)
findings.body: `unsubscribe` changes the user's notification level, but it is routed as a plain GET (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`) with no token or confirmation, and `check_xhr` is skipped. Any page or forum post the logged-in user's browser loads can trigger it, for example a post containing `![](/t/foo/123/unsubscribe)`. Every viewer is then silently demoted on topic 123, and after a second load they are muted. The `TopicUser` update runs before `respond_to`, so it is saved even when the request is an image fetch. Existing mutations such as `mute`/`unmute`/`set_notifications` use PUT/POST. Fix: make the mutation a POST from the Ember page, or require a signed per-user key in the URL.

findings.title: NoMethodError when the user has no TopicUser row
findings.body: `TopicUser.find_by(user_id:, topic_id:)` returns nil when the logged-in user has never interacted with the topic. Examples: a forwarded link, a guessed URL, or the embedded-image case. The next line, `tu.notification_level`, then raises and the request returns a 500. Use `TopicUser.change`, which creates the row if missing, or handle nil explicitly.

findings.title: Direct `tu.save!` bypasses TopicUser.change, so the unsubscribe can be silently reverted
findings.body:
Assigning `notification_level` and calling `save!` skips what `TopicUser.change` does: setting `notifications_reason_id = user_changed` and `notifications_changed_at`, and publishing the MessageBus `notification_level_change`.

Users who were auto-tracked through `update_last_read` have `notifications_reason_id` NULL. For them, both `update_last_read` (`case when tu.notifications_reason_id is null and ... then :tracking`) and `TopicUser.auto_track` will bump the level back to tracking on the next read or post, undoing the unsubscribe.

Other open tabs also never learn about the change because nothing is published on MessageBus. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)`.

findings.title: Toggle logic does not stop the emails it promises to stop, and repeat visits escalate to muted
findings.body:
If the level is above regular it drops only to regular; otherwise it mutes.

Reply, mention and quote emails are also sent at the regular level. A tracking user who clicks the link in a 'replied' email ends up at regular and keeps receiving exactly those emails. Meanwhile the page tells them 'You will stop receiving notifications for <title>'.

The action is also not idempotent. Refreshing the page, a browser prefetch, or clicking a second email link moves the user one more step down, from regular to muted. The intended target level should be explicit, for example always muted, or at least below the level that triggers the email type that was clicked.

findings.title: Explicit `render :show` happens before `show` sets canonical_url, dropping the topic canonical link
findings.body:
`perform_show_response` now calls `render :show` inside `format.html`. Rails renders the template and layout immediately at that call.

In `show`, `canonical_url UrlHelper.absolute_without_cdn(...)` runs afterwards (line 87). Previously the implicit render happened at the end of the action, so `@canonical_url` was already set. Now the layout's canonical link tag is rendered without it and falls back to the request path. Post-number URLs like `/t/slug/123/45` then advertise themselves as canonical, which is an SEO and duplicate-content regression. Move the `canonical_url` call before `perform_show_response`, or set it inside it.

findings.title: Client-side transition to the unsubscribe route shows the confirmation without unsubscribing
findings.body:
The route's model hook calls `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)`. That uses the preloaded `topic_<id>` payload, or otherwise fetches `/t/<id>.json`; it never hits `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe`.

Only a full page load reaches `TopicsController#unsubscribe`. If the user reaches this route through in-app navigation, or once the preload has been consumed, the page claims 'You will stop receiving notifications' but no server-side change is made.

findings.title: Logged-out users clicking the email link lose the unsubscribe intent
findings.body: `unsubscribe` was added to `ensure_logged_in`. Many recipients click email links on a device where they are not logged in. For a non-XHR GET, the NotLoggedIn handling sends them to the homepage, with no return-to path and no message. The unsubscribe silently does not happen, and the user has no indication they need to log in and retry.

findings.title: add_unsubscribe_link now implicitly requires unsubscribe_url
findings.body:
The `unsubscribe_link` translation now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. Any caller (core or plugin) that passes `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url` will hit `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` in both `body` (line 90) and `html_part`. The spec had to be changed to pass a dummy URL for this reason.

The text 'stop receiving notifications about this particular topic' also only makes sense for topic emails. Consider a separate translation key, appended only when `unsubscribe_url` is present.

findings.title: No tests for the new unsubscribe endpoint or for the per-topic link in emails
findings.body:
The only spec change passes a dummy `unsubscribe_url` so the existing test does not crash. Nothing asserts that the URL actually appears in the body or HTML part.

There are no controller specs for `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, covering:
- the level transitions (watching/tracking to regular, regular to muted),
- the slug redirect,
- the missing-TopicUser case,
- the logged-out case.

Those are where the bugs above live.
